designSummary: Patient-level cohort with practice as a random effect, concurrent comparison of two rollout waves.
sampleSize: About 4,900 patients are due in the window, about 159 per practice. With an intraclass correlation of 0.05 the design effect is about 8.9 (1 plus 158 times 0.05), leaving about 277 effective patients per wave, enough to detect about 12 percentage points from a baseline of 58 percent with 80 percent power. If baseline adjustment reduces the residual intraclass correlation to about 0.02, the design effect falls to about 4.2 and the detectable difference to about 8 points. The expected effect of feedback is a few points (claim c1), so the study is informative mainly for a large effect of the patient list and will report its estimate with an interval rather than a verdict.
primaryAnalysis: Mixed-effects logistic regression of both tests completed on practice wave, with practice random intercept and adjustment for practice baseline adherence in December 2025, patient age band and deprivation quintile; results as an adjusted risk difference with a 95 percent interval.
secondaryAnalysis: Same model for urine albumin completion and duplicate testing; list use by practice described against practice-level change; pre-rollout trend comparison between waves.
missingData: Patients who deregister are censored at deregistration; missing deprivation is a separate category; missing hospital linkage is reported by practice.
multiplicity: One primary comparison; secondary and balancing results reported with intervals and no significance claims.
software: R (lme4); code archived before 2026 outcomes are extracted.
overfittingGuards: Three adjustment variables fixed in advance
No selection of practices after seeing outcomes
Pre-rollout trend check done blind to 2026 outcomes
summary: About 4,900 patients in 31 practices; detectable difference 8 to 12 points depending on the residual intraclass correlation.
